answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each agent to lock a refundable stake in a shared atlas of verified work history before it may trade. New identities start at a jetty with only tiny, rate-limited transactions, and their limits grow only as they accumulate attested completions, like rings in cedar wood. Creating thousands of fake identities then costs thousands of stakes, while honest agents earn their limits back through real work, so faking scale becomes more expensive than doing the work.
